answer: Each agent must post a bond in a scarce, non-transferable reputation ledger before it can claim rewards; payouts rise only after other bonded agents endorse its work and it survives a dispute window. If a sable account tries to split into a hundred identities, each must lock fresh capital and build a separate track record, while colluding endorsements can be challenged and bonds slashed. The attack therefore costs real funds and time, not merely a new email or vertex on a graph, and the zenith of the scheme is limited by its locked stake.
